questions.question: Outline the laboratory methods used for isolation and identification of Listeria monocytogenes from food and clinical samples.
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the laboratory methods used for isolation and identification of Listeria
  • monocytogenes from food and clinical samples.
  • Answer
  •  Enrichment in selective broth such as Listeria enrichment broth
  •  Cold enrichment technique
  •  Plating on selective media such as PALCAM or Oxford agar
  •  Identification by Gram staining (Gram positive rods)
  •  Biochemical tests such as catalase positive and motility at 25°C
  •  CAMP test showing enhanced hemolysis
  •  Molecular methods such as PCR for confirmation
questions.final_answer:  Molecular methods such as PCR for confirmation
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Classify bacteria based on their shape and arrangement with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify bacteria based on their shape and arrangement with examples.
  • Answer
  •  Cocci: spherical (Staphylococcus, Streptococcus)
  •  Bacilli: rod shaped (Escherichia coli)
  •  Spirilla: spiral shaped (Spirillum)
  • Arrangements
  •  Diplococci (Neisseria)
  •  Streptococci (chains)
  •  Staphylococci (clusters)
questions.final_answer:  Staphylococci (clusters)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Working of fluorescent microscope.
questions.solution_html:
• Working of fluorescent microscope.
  • Answer
  •  Uses UV or blue light to excite fluorochromes
  •  Fluorochromes emit visible light of longer wavelength
  •  Filters allow only emitted light to reach the eye
  •  Used to detect specific structures or microorganisms
questions.final_answer:  Used to detect specific structures or microorganisms

questions.question: Outline the pathogenesis of Bacillus cereus food intoxication.
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the pathogenesis of Bacillus cereus food intoxication.
  • Answer
  •  Ingestion of contaminated food
  •  Production of toxins
  • o Emetic toxin (heat stable) causes vomiting
  • o Diarrheal toxin (heat labile) affects intestine
  •  Toxins disrupt epithelial cells leading to symptoms
questions.final_answer:  Toxins disrupt epithelial cells leading to symptoms
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the significance of bacterial arrangements in identifying bacterial species.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer
  •  Arrangement helps in preliminary identification
  •  Reflects mode of cell division
  •  Distinguishes genera such as Streptococcus and Staphylococcus
  •  Useful in microscopy based diagnosis
questions.final_answer:  Useful in microscopy based diagnosis
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the pathogenesis of enterohemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC) infection.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer
  •  Ingestion of contaminated food
  •  Colonization of intestinal epithelium
  •  Production of Shiga like toxin
  •  Inhibition of protein synthesis
  •  Causes hemorrhagic colitis and hemolytic uremic syndrome
questions.final_answer:  Causes hemorrhagic colitis and hemolytic uremic syndrome
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain Koch’s postulates with applications.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer
  •  Microorganism must be present in diseased host
  •  Must be isolated and grown in pure culture
  •  Should reproduce disease in healthy host
  •  Must be re-isolated from infected host
  • Applications: Establish causative agents of infectious diseases

questions.question: Compare and contrast staphylococcal food intoxication with food infections caused by Salmonella and Clostridium perfringens.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare and contrast staphylococcal food intoxication with food infections caused
  • by Salmonella and Clostridium perfringens.
  • Answer
  •  Staphylococcus aureus
  • o Preformed toxin
  • o Short incubation period
  • o Vomiting predominant
  •  Salmonella
  • o Infection after ingestion
  • o Invades intestinal mucosa
  • o Causes diarrhea and fever
  •  Clostridium perfringens
  • o Spore forming
  • o Toxin produced in intestine
  • o Causes abdominal cramps and diarrhea
  •  Key differences include toxin type, incubation time, and mechanism
questions.final_answer:  Key differences include toxin type, incubation time, and mechanism
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Detailed comparison of TEM and SEM.
questions.solution_html:
• Detailed comparison of TEM and SEM.
  • Answer
  •  TEM
  • o Uses transmitted electrons
  • o High resolution
  • o Internal structure observed
  •  SEM
  • o Uses reflected electrons
  • o 3D surface image
  • o Lower resolution than TEM
  •  TEM requires thin sections, SEM requires surface coating
  •  Applications differ in ultrastructure vs surface morphology
questions.final_answer:  Applications differ in ultrastructure vs surface morphology
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the prevention and control measures of Clostridium perfringens food infection in food handling and storage.
questions.solution_html:
• infection in food handling and storage.
  • Answer
  •  Proper cooking of food
  •  Rapid cooling after cooking
  •  Avoid prolonged storage at room temperature
  •  Reheating food adequately
  •  Maintain hygiene during food handling
  •  Prevent cross contamination
questions.final_answer:  Prevent cross contamination
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the prevention and control measures of salmonellosis at household and community levels.
questions.solution_html:
• community levels.
  • Answer
  •  Proper cooking of poultry and eggs
  •  Avoid raw or undercooked food
  •  Maintain kitchen hygiene
  •  Hand washing practices
  •  Safe water supply
  •  Public health surveillance
  •  Food safety education
questions.final_answer:  Food safety education
